chunks: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub, from al-'Abbas ibn Musa, from Yunus ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Sinan ibn Tarif, who said:
I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about a man who sold his wife.

He عليه السلام said: "The man's hand is to be cut off; the woman is to be stoned if intercourse was committed with her; and the one who bought her, if he had intercourse with her and was muhsan, is to be stoned if he knew of that; and if he was not muhsan, he is to be given one hundred lashes."

key_terms.تُقْطَعَ يَدُهُ: his hand is to be amputated as punishment
key_terms.مُحْصَنًا: legally married / sexually safeguarded person subject to the ruling of rajm
key_terms.وُطِئَتْ: sexual intercourse was committed with her

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling in Shia hadith on a man who sells his wife and on the buyer who has intercourse with her?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the grave offense of a man purporting to sell his wife and the unlawful intercourse that may follow from it. It outlines distinct hadd punishments for the seller, the woman if intercourse occurred, and the buyer depending on his knowledge and marital status.
